title: Decoupling CO2 Emissions and Economic Growth Across the U.S
content: Abstract: To mitigate climate change, it will be necessary to decouple greenhouse gas emissions and economic development. We explore trends in CO2/GDP as an indicator of decoupling. CO2/GDP is most often studied at the national level, but data are available for the 2010-2015 time period to explore the indicator at both the state and county scales in the U.S. County-level data reveal large heterogeneity with adjacent counties often exhibiting very different trends and many states showing diverse patterns of change. Although CO2 emissions have been decreasing as GDP increases in the U.S. as a whole, the same is true in only four-fifths of its states and in only around one-third of its counties. There are many counties in which CO2 is increasing as GDP declines, or in other combinations. Decoupling of CO2 emissions and economic growth are most apparent in counties with a large fraction of their emissions coming from electricity generation while decou-pling is less common in counties with large emissions from the industrial sector. Counties from large urban concentrations are also more likely to be decoupling. The spatial heterogeneity at the county level suggests the variety and challenges in motivating the decoupling of emissions from economic growth.
